readings.title: Job Continues His Lament
readings.subtitle: My Spirit Is Broken
readings.text: [Job 17:1] “My spirit is broken, my days are extinguished, the graves are ready for me. [2] “Are not mockers with me? And does not my eye watch their provocation? [3] “Please lay down a pledge for me with <dn>Yourself</dn>. Who is there that strikes hands with me? [4] “For <dn>You</dn> have hidden their heart from understanding, therefore <dn>You</dn> do not exalt them. [5] “He who denounces friends for a portion, even the eyes of his children fail. [6] “But <dn>He</dn> has made me a byword of the people, and I am one in whose face they spit. [7] “And from sorrow my eye has grown dim, and all my members are like a shadow. [8] “Upright ones are astonished at this, and the innocent stirs himself up against the profane. [9] “But the righteous holds to his way, and he who has clean hands becomes stronger and stronger. [10] “But please, come back again, all of you, for I do not find a wise one among you. [11] “My days have passed, my plans are broken off – the possessions of my heart. [12] “They treat night as day, saying, ‘Light is near,’ in the face of darkness. [13] “If I wait for She’ol as my house, if I make my bed in the darkness, [14] “If I call to the pit, ‘You are my father’; to the worm, ‘You are my mother and my sister,’ [15] “Where then is my expectation? As for my expectation, who looks for it? [16] “Will they go down to the gates of She’ol? Shall we have rest together in the dust?”

readings.title: Bildad’s Second Speech
readings.subtitle: The Light of the Wicked Shall Be Put Out
readings.text: [Job 18:1] Then Bildad the Shuḥite answered and said, [2] “How long until you make an end of words? Understand, and afterwards let us speak. [3] “Why are we reckoned as beasts, and regarded as stupid in your sight? [4] “He tears himself in his displeasure! Is the earth left for your sake? Or is the rock moved from its place? [5] “The light of the wicked is certainly put out, and the spark of his fire does not shine. [6] “The light shall be dark in his tent, and his lamp beside him is put out. [7] “The steps of his strength are hampered, and his own counsel casts him down. [8] “For he is sent into a net by his own feet, and he walks on a snare. [9] “A gin takes him by the heel, a trap lays hold of him. [10] “A noose is hidden for him on the ground, and a snare for him on the path. [11] “Terrors frighten him on every side, and drive him to his feet. [12] “His strength is starved, and destruction is ready at his side. [13] “It consumes the parts of his skin; the first-born of death consumes his parts. [14] “He is torn from his tent, his trust, and it marches him to the sovereign of terrors. [15] “There dwells in his tent what is none of his; sulphur is scattered on his home. [16] “His roots are dried up below, and his branch is cut off above. [17] “His remembrance perishes from the earth, and he has no name on the street. [18] “They drive him from light into darkness, and chase him out of the world. [19] “He has neither son nor descendant among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings. [20] “Those coming after shall be astonished at his day, as those going before were seized with fright. [21] “Truly such are the dwellings of the perverse, and this is the place of him who does not know <dn>El</dn>.”

readings.title: Job Answers Bildad
readings.subtitle: My Redeemer Lives
readings.text: [Job 19:1] Then Iyyoḇ answered and said, [2] “How long will you grieve my being, and crush me with words? [3] “These ten times you have reproached me; you are not ashamed that you attack me. [4] “And also, if I have truly strayed, my straying remains with me. [5] “If indeed you exalt yourselves against me, and plead my disgrace against me, [6] “Know then that <dn>Eloah</dn> has overthrown me, and has surrounded me with <dn>His</dn> net. [7] “See, I cry out, ‘Violence!’ but I am not answered; I cry aloud, but there is no right-ruling. [8] “<dn>He</dn> has fenced up my way so that I cannot pass, and <dn>He</dn> sets darkness on my paths. [9] “<dn>He</dn> has stripped me of my esteem, and taken the crown from my head. [10] “<dn>He</dn> breaks me down on every side, and I am gone; and my expectation <dn>He</dn> has uprooted like a tree. [11] “And <dn>He</dn> kindles <dn>His</dn> wrath against me, and <dn>He</dn> counts me as one of <dn>His</dn> enemies. [12] “<dn>His</dn> troops come together and build up their way against me, and they encamp round about my tent. [13] “<dn>He</dn> has removed my brothers far from me, and those who know me have completely turned away from me. [14] “My relatives have failed, and my close friends have forgotten me. [15] “Those dwelling in my house and my female servants count me as a stranger; I am an alien in their eyes. [16] “I call my servant, but he gives no answer; I beg him with my mouth. [17] “My breath is strange to my wife, and I am loathsome to the children of my own body. [18] “Even young children despise me; I arise, and they speak against me. [19] “All my inward friends abominate me, and those whom I love have turned against me. [20] “My bone clings to my skin and to my flesh, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth. [21] “Show me favour, show me favour, O you my friends, for the hand of <dn>Eloah</dn> has struck me! [22] “Why do you persecute me as <dn>El</dn> does, and are not satisfied with my flesh? [23] “Oh, that my words were written! Oh, that they were inscribed in a book! [24] “That they were engraved on a rock with an iron pen and lead, forever! [25] “For I know that my Redeemer lives, and as the Last shall rise over the dust; [26] “And after my skin has been destroyed, this: that in my flesh I shall see <dn>Eloah</dn>, [27] “Whom I, for myself, shall see, and my eyes shall see, and not another. My kidneys are consumed within me. [28] “If you say, ‘How shall we persecute him?’ Since the root of the matter is found in me, [29] “Fear the sword for yourselves, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, that you might know there is a judgment.”

readings.title: Zophar’s Second Speech
readings.subtitle: The Triumph of the Wicked Is Short
readings.text: [Job 20:1] Then Tsophar the Na‛amathite answered and said, [2] “Therefore my anxious thoughts answer me, because of my feelings within me. [3] “I have heard the reproof that puts me to shame, and the spirit of my understanding answers me. [4] “Do you know this of old, since man was placed on earth, [5] “That the singing of the wrong is short, and the joy of the profane is but for a moment? [6] “Though his excellence mounts up to the heavens, and his head reaches to the clouds, [7] “Like his own dung he perishes forever; those who have seen him say, ‘Where is he?’ [8] “He flies away like a dream, and is not found; and he is chased away like a vision of the night. [9] “The eye that saw him sees him no more, and his place beholds him no more. [10] “His children seek the favour of the poor, and his hands give back his wealth. [11] “His bones are full of his youth, but it lies down with him in the dust. [12] “Though evil is sweet in his mouth, and he hides it under his tongue, [13] “Though he spares it and does not forsake it, but keeps it in his mouth, [14] “His food in his stomach shall be turned, it becomes cobra gall within him. [15] “He swallows down riches and vomits them up again; <dn>El</dn> casts them out of his belly. [16] “He sucks the poison of cobras; the tongue of the viper slays him. [17] “He does not look on the floods, the rivers, the streams of honey and curds. [18] “He restores what he laboured for and does not swallow it; according to the wealth of his trade, he does not rejoice. [19] “Because he has oppressed and forsaken the poor, he has seized a house which he did not build. [20] “Because he knew no ease in his belly, he does not save what he desired. [21] “There is no remnant of his food, therefore his good does not last. [22] “In the fullness of his sufficiency he is in distress; every hand of the miserable comes against him. [23] “It comes to be: to fill his belly, <dn>He</dn> sends on him the burning of <dn>His</dn> wrath, and rains it on him while he is eating. [24] “He flees from the iron weapon; a bow of bronze pierces him through. [25] “It is drawn, and comes out of the body; and the glittering point comes out of his gall; terrors come upon him. [26] “All darkness is hidden for his treasures; a fire not blown consumes him; it goes badly with the remnant in his tent. [27] “The heavens reveal his crookedness, and the earth rises up against him. [28] “The increase of his house departs, flowing away in the day of <dn>His</dn> wrath. [29] “This is the portion from <dn>Elohim</dn> for a wrong man, and the heritage appointed to him by <dn>El</dn>.”

readings.title: Job Answers Zophar
readings.subtitle: Why Do the Wicked Prosper?
readings.text: [Job 21:1] And Iyyoḇ answered and said, [2] “Listen closely to my speech, and let this be your consolation. [3] “Bear with me that I may speak; and after I have spoken, mock on. [4] “As for me, is my complaint against man? And if it were, why should my spirit not be impatient? [5] “Turn to me and be astonished, and lay your hand over your mouth. [6] “Even when I remember I am afraid, and trembling takes hold of my flesh. [7] “Why do the wicked live, become old, indeed become mighty in power? [8] “Their seed is established with them in their sight, and their offspring before their eyes. [9] “Their houses are safe from fear, and the rod of <dn>Eloah</dn> is not on them. [10] “His bull breeds without fail; his cow calves and does not miscarry. [11] “They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance. [12] “They sing to the timbrel and lyre, and rejoice at the sound of the flute. [13] “They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to She’ol. [14] “And they say to <dn>El</dn>, ‘Depart from us, for we have no desire to know <dn>Your</dn> ways. [15] ‘Who is the <dn>Almighty</dn>, that we should serve <dn>Him</dn>? And what do we profit if we pray to <dn>Him</dn>?’ [16] “See, their good is not in their hand. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.

readings.title: The Wicked and Their End
readings.subtitle: One Dies in Strength, Another in Bitterness
readings.text: [Job 21:17] “How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? And their calamity comes upon them? <dn>He</dn> apportions pangs in <dn>His</dn> displeasure. [18] “They are as straw before the wind, and like chaff that a storm steals away. [19] “<dn>Eloah</dn> stores up his punishment for his children; let <dn>Him</dn> repay him so that he knows it. [20] “Let his eyes see his destruction, and let him drink of the wrath of the <dn>Almighty</dn>. [21] “For what is his delight in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off? [22] “Does one teach <dn>El</dn> knowledge, since <dn>He</dn> judges those on high? [23] “One dies in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet. [24] “His pails are full of milk, and the marrow of his bones is moist. [25] “And another dies in the bitterness of his being, and has not eaten with pleasure. [26] “They lie down alike in the dust, and worms cover them. [27] “See, I know your thoughts, and the schemes with which you would wrong me. [28] “For you say, ‘Where is the house of the noble? And where is the tent of the dwelling places of the wicked?’ [29] “Have you not asked those who pass by the way? And do you not know their signs? [30] “That the wicked is preserved for the day of calamity? They are brought out for the day of wrath. [31] “Who declares his way to his face? And who repays him for what he has done? [32] “Yet he is brought to the grave, and a watch is kept over the tomb. [33] “The clods of the valley shall be sweet to him; and all men draw after him, as there were innumerable before him. [34] “How then do you comfort me with emptiness, since in your answers there remains only trespass?”
